newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota soy harvest progresses, corn still wet.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota soy harvest progresses, corn still wet.

text.p: The soybean harvest made "excellent" progress in the week ended Sunday, but most corn continued to be too wet to combine, South Dakota's Agricultural Statistics Service said in a weekly report.
It said the soybean harvest jumped 38 points to 84 percent completed despite being hampered by midweek rain. That was ahead of the five-year average of 72 percent.
Corn was 19 percent harvested, compared with seven percent percent last week and 36 percent for the five-year average.
Many producers reported that the moisture content was still above 25 percent and that a hard freeze was needed in some areas to help dry it down, the report said.
Corn was rated one percent poor, 13 percent fair, 63 percent good and 23 percent excellent. Soybeans were rated two percent poor, 18 percent fair, 58 percent good and 22 percent excellent.

Winter wheat was 97 percent seeded, behind average of 100 percent. Some farmers in the north central and central parts of the state were still seeding and some producers said it was the latest they had ever seeded their winter wheat.
Soil moisture rated nil very short, two percent short, 79 percent adequate and 19 percent surplus.
